h: Knebworth, lakes and more around Stevenage
p: A couple of planning thoughts before you head over. Toddlers and pre-schoolers usually have the most fun in the morning, when they're fresh and the place is calmer. If you've got school-age kids, school holidays will be busier, so get there early if you can.

Socks are a must at play centres, so pop a pair in the bag for everyone, plus a spare set of clothes for any messy moments. A drink bottle each and a few snacks will keep everyone happy and save trips to the counter.
With siblings of different ages, try letting each child choose an area in turn. It keeps things fair and stops the younger ones being dragged around after the bigger kids.

Stevenage was the first of Britain's post-war new towns, and it's surrounded by green space that's perfect for an afternoon outside. Fairlands Valley Park is a big park in the middle of the town, with lakes, open grass and plenty of room to run, making it a brilliant place to wind down after a morning indoors.

Knebworth House, on the edge of Stevenage, is a grand country house with gardens and parkland, and it's well known for hosting big outdoor concerts over the years. It's a lovely day out in its own right for families who fancy a bit of history and countryside.
For something more low-key, Stevenage Old Town has a traditional high street with independent shops, cafés and pubs, a nice contrast to the modern town centre.
